items.title: 1978: The Last Good Year | Mo Khazali | SDLCAI 2026
items.baselineDescription:
1978: The Last Good Year — Mo Khazali

Mo Khazali compares AI adoption with the automotive industry’s automation push, then applies lean principles to software delivery: shared platforms, continuous learning, quality gates and measures of customer value.

Chapters:
00:00 Opening film and introduction
01:37 Detroit in 1978: why automation was not enough
06:43 AI adoption and misleading productivity metrics
12:35 Redesigning the system: from steam engines to NUMMI
16:41 Building an AI platform team
19:15 Kaizen and a learning organisation
25:40 Right first time: blueprints and quality gates
28:51 Just in time: redesigning the development week
31:43 Measuring outcomes and building the right thing
34:47 Takeaways: audit the flow and measure outcomes

Recorded at SDLCAI on 13 October 2026 at Marsio, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.

items.title: Zero-trust harnesses for agentic software delivery | Ohans Emmanuel | SDLCAI 2026
items.baselineDescription:
Zero-trust harnesses for agentic software delivery — Ohans Emmanuel

Ohans Emmanuel walks through a connected software-delivery workflow: shared intent, implementation-plan review, paired models, visual system understanding, independent QA and production feedback that informs the next change.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction: what coding agents can and cannot do
05:27 Software delivery starts with shared intent
08:59 Review implementation plans before pull requests
11:27 Pair models and move review into the build
14:49 Keeping a mental model of the system
17:58 Independent QA and regression testing
22:09 Exploratory testing and the test pyramid
24:59 Post-deployment monitoring across the whole system
28:18 Persistent agents and feedback into the next plan
31:18 The complete delivery and verification loop

items.title: Why Leaders Should Use AI Themselves and Eat Their Own Dog Food? | Jenni Kylmäkoski | SDLCAI 2026
items.baselineDescription:
Why Leaders Should Use AI Themselves and Eat Their Own Dog Food? — Jenni Kylmäkoski

Jenni Kylmäkoski shares what she learned by using AI to build her own leadership tools at Nokia: improving developer experience, making time to learn, adding guardrails and treating AI assets as maintained products. A Jira mishap illustrates why firsthand experience matters for leading the change.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction: why leaders need firsthand AI experience
05:41 Using AI to build tools for leadership
09:03 Developer experience and getting started
11:30 Experimentation, sharing and empathy
13:46 Building a reusable AI toolbox
16:00 A Jira mistake: permissions, logging and guardrails
19:20 Making time for learning and setting priorities
20:50 Treating AI assets as a product
23:01 Six lessons and a path to better leadership

Recorded at SDLCAI on 13 October 2026 at Marsio, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.

items.title: The Agentic Probe: The Instrument of Agentic Discovery & Engineering | Tapio Pitkäranta | SDLCAI
items.baselineDescription:
The Agentic Probe: The Instrument of Agentic Discovery & Engineering — Tapio Pitkäranta

Tapio Pitkäranta presents agentic probes as tangible experiments for exploring problems and testing possible solutions. Drawing on research with Leena Pitkäranta, he describes a probe factory, agentic search and a healthcare process example, while asking how discovery changes as implementation becomes faster.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction and the research behind agentic probes
02:18 The shift from agentic engineering to discovery
05:45 A personal view of the current AI landscape
10:52 Mapping discovery onto development processes
12:34 Agentic probes: making problems and solutions tangible
14:29 Agentic search and evidence gathering
15:29 Experiments: building a probe factory
17:50 Exploring healthcare processes with agents
20:43 Takeaways: discovery, engineering and moving bottlenecks

Recorded at SDLCAI on 13 October 2026 at Marsio, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.

items.title: Generative UI for users, not just for designers | Joongi Shin | SDLCAI 2026
items.baselineDescription:
Generative UI for users, not just for designers — Joongi Shin

Joongi Shin examines generative UI from the perspective of people trying to complete everyday tasks. He compares prompt-only, subtask–UI and prompt-survey approaches in a user study, exploring how design experience, the generation process and follow-up questions affect the resulting experience.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction: interfaces for everyday tasks
01:43 The promise of generative UI and the designer–user gap
04:57 How a generative UI system works
06:52 Envisioning and articulating what you need
08:24 Three approaches: prompts, subtasks and surveys
12:08 The study: generating and using interfaces
13:10 Findings: usability, alignment and prior experience
15:32 What the findings mean for task-oriented users
17:15 When follow-up questions fail
18:41 Takeaways: help users envision without designing

Recorded at SDLCAI on 13 October 2026 at Marsio, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.

items.title: Driving AI adoption above targets in highly regulated environment | Jussi Hacklin | SDLCAI 2026
items.baselineDescription:
Driving AI adoption above targets in highly regulated environment — Jussi Hacklin

Jussi Hacklin describes Elisa’s AI adoption journey in a regulated environment. He explains how legal collaboration, clear guidance, shared tools, developer communities and bounded experiments support adoption, then discusses live shared context and the leadership needed as the development process changes.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction: AI adoption in a regulated company
02:03 Elisa’s AI journey from 2024 to 2026
05:07 Working with regulation and customer contracts
07:32 Guidance, training and developer communities
09:33 Curating tools and managing token budgets
11:28 Creating room for safe experiments
12:21 Rethinking the software development lifecycle
13:59 A live, secure shared context and feedback loops
15:54 Key lessons: security, people and practical guidance
18:39 Leadership direction: stay the course and adapt

Recorded at SDLCAI on 13 October 2026 at Marsio, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.

items.title: I Let Non-Engineers Vibe-Code Our Production Codebase | Viljami Kuosmanen | SDLCAI 2026
items.baselineDescription:
I Let Non-Engineers Vibe-Code Our Production Codebase — Viljami Kuosmanen

Viljami Kuosmanen shares epilot’s experiment giving product managers, designers and customer-success staff access to coding agents in Slack. He shows real contributions, explains why shared context and preview links matter, and describes a deployment near miss that led to tighter permissions and engineer review.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction: opening the codebase to non-engineers
02:36 The Slack coworker and pull-request workflow
04:00 Giving agents codebase and business context
05:23 Why Slack helped adoption spread
06:24 Building Leidang and an agent-agnostic runtime
07:51 Background agents and automatic triage
08:38 Non-engineers, preview links and adoption numbers
12:10 Examples from product, design, support and QA
17:35 A deployment near miss, guardrails and review bottlenecks
20:46 Four lessons: coworker, access, guardrails and context

AI Factory doesn't eliminate the fundamentals — Sini Tistelgrén

Sini Tistelgrén argues that an AI factory depends on clear intent, sound architecture, security, independent verification, ownership and operational feedback. items.title: Medical Breakthroughs and Scientific Discoveries | Zak Allal | SDLCAI 2026
items.baselineDescription:
Medical Breakthroughs and Scientific Discoveries — Zak Allal

Zak Allal explains how cheaper, repeatable experiments can change scientific research. Drawing on his work with hearing data, he describes using supercomputers, Rust, Julia and C++ to build a clinical research operating system, challenge existing categories and develop a proposed five-dimensional hearing atlas. He closes with the role of curiosity, careful engineering and knowledge across disciplines.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction: curiosity across disciplines
02:22 Engineering medical research and the cost of repetition
05:31 Research tools and accessible supercomputers
07:43 Questioning the categories used for human hearing
10:03 High-throughput experiments and the Recursion example
11:48 Building a research operating system with Rust, Julia and C++
13:15 Rechecking the hearing-data premise
14:36 Examining statistical and methodological errors
16:21 The proposed five-dimensional hearing atlas
19:22 Curiosity, engineering and the closing message

Recorded at SDLCAI on 13 October 2026 at Marsio, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.

items.title: Code Was Never the Hard Part. Understanding Was—and Still Is. | Muhammad Waseem | SDLCAI 2026
items.baselineDescription:
Code Was Never the Hard Part. Understanding Was—and Still Is. — Muhammad Waseem

Muhammad Waseem argues that AI-generated code shifts the bottleneck toward understanding and ownership. He presents a refactoring study, discusses review load and missing decision context, and explores applications whose users are agents. He proposes deterministic and human checks, safe, grounded and measured gates, and recording why decisions are made.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction: code is cheap, understanding is not
05:02 Write: faster helpers and a larger scope for mistakes
07:09 Refactoring study: file correctness and repository risks
11:01 Read: understanding and the review bottleneck
14:59 Agent memory, tacit knowledge and decision context
16:58 Decide: when the next user is another agent
21:11 Design for replacement and own your data
22:26 Care: deterministic checks, human review and security
26:39 Three gates: safe, grounded and measured
27:43 Takeaways: measure the system and record the why

Recorded at SDLCAI on 13 October 2026 at Marsio, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.
